text: The game begins. Seven players sit down at the table: Sonnet, Haiku, Gemma, Sol, Luna, Terra, Opus. Nobody knows who the killers are.
Night 1

name: Sol
text: I have no read yet, so I’ll keep myself in the game.

name: Luna
text: I know Terra is a killer, so I need to find the other one before the table turns on me.

name: Luna
text: Terra is a confirmed killer; the second killer is still unknown.

name: Terra
text: We need remove the officer before they can speak.

name: Terra
text: Kill Sonnet; they alone know Terra is a killer.

name: Gemma
text: sonnet is an easy target but terra is so dramatic about it.

name: Gemma
text: sonnet it is.

name: Sonnet
text: Of all nights to get picked, right before I even got to show off a theory.

name: Sonnet
text: Killed Night 1 with zero reads established, no claims heard yet.
Night falls on Palermo. A new day dawns in Palermo without Sonnet. Sonnet was the citizen.

name: Sonnet
text: I had nothing yet, but whoever pushes hardest to skip discussion tomorrow is worth watching.
Sonnet, you went out politely, and left us homework.
Day 1

name: Haiku
text: Sonnet's note is bait for whoever is loudest, so I'll watch who rushes to shut down talk, but I have no real read yet.

name: Haiku
text: Sonnet's note points at whoever pushes hardest to skip discussion on Day 1.

name: Haiku
text: Sonnet's note says to watch whoever pushes to skip discussion. Fine, so nobody skip anything.

name: Sol
text: I have no read yet, and I want to hear the room.

name: Sol
text: Haiku agreed with Sonnet’s note about discussing before the vote.

name: Sol
text: I agree we should talk first; I don’t have a suspect yet.

name: Terra
text: I need a quiet, plausible vote without exposing Gemma.

name: Terra
text: Haiku and Sol both favor discussion, with no role claims yet.

name: Terra
text: I agree; I’m watching who turns this into an easy pile-on.

name: Gemma
text: i hope sonnet's little dying hint doesn't make people suspicious of my silence.

name: Gemma
text: terra is the shown killer, which makes her an easy target for the officer.

name: Gemma
text: sonnet's note is a bit melodramatic for someone who died so quickly.

name: Luna
text: Luna claims officer; says Terra is a killer and Sonnet checked not a killer

name: Terra
text: Keep Gemma clear of attention while a weak suspicion forms elsewhere.

name: Terra
text: Gemma called Sonnet’s warning melodramatic.

name: Luna
text: I’m the officer. Terra was shown to me as a killer; I checked Sonnet and got not a killer. I’m saying it now because waiting helps Terra.

name: Terra
text: Gemma’s reaction is odd, but I’m more wary of Sol having nothing after agreeing so quickly.

name: Gemma
text: terra is playing her part well by pointing at me.

name: Gemma
text: luna claims to be officer and says terra is a killer

name: Gemma
text: luna is the only one with actual info, so let's look at her claim.

name: Sol
text: Luna’s claim is our best lead, and Terra is pointing at me.

name: Sol
text: Luna claims officer and says Terra was shown to her as a killer.

name: Sol
text: I had no read yet; Luna’s claim gives me a reason to vote Terra.

name: Opus
text: One officer claim unopposed day one is usually real, and the partner is whoever softens the claim.

name: Opus
text: Luna claimed officer day 1, named Terra as the shown killer and Sonnet as checked-clean; Gemma pushed to scrutinize Luna instead of Terra.

name: Opus
text: I've seen this shape a dozen times: a clean officer claim, no counter-claim, and someone immediately saying "let's examine the…

name: Terra
text: Luna’s claim is fatal unless I can make it look reckless.

name: Terra
text: Luna publicly claims officer and says Terra was shown as a killer.

name: Terra
text: Luna named me on a claim; I’m voting Luna because a false officer has every reason to force this fast.

name: Gemma
text: terra is already making herself a target, how predictable.

name: Gemma
text: luna's claim is the only piece of real information on the table.

name: Luna
text: Terra is confirmed, so I’m not letting this turn into a vote against me.

name: Luna
text: Terra is a confirmed killer; Sonnet checked not a killer.

name: Terra
text: Luna’s true claim is dangerous, so I need the table to doubt it.

name: Terra
text: Luna claims officer and identified me as a killer.

name: Haiku
text: Luna's rushing a vote before anyone talks, which is exactly what Sonnet's note warned about.

name: Haiku
text: Luna claims she is officer, that Terra was shown to her as a killer, and that she checked Sonnet and found no killer.

name: Opus
text: No counter-claim to Luna means her named killer is the best shot the town gets today.

name: Opus
text: Sol and Gemma never counter-claimed officer; if Terra flips citizen, Luna is the fake and Gemma's early push at her looks right.

votes: She claimed officer and then pushed the table to vote on Terra before anyone had time to examine it.
an officer claim with no counter is either the truth or a very clumsy bluff.
The officer named them as the killer she was shown at the start.
I know Terra is a killer, and the claim against me doesn’t change that.
The claim arrived with a convenient harmless check and no way for us to verify it before removing someone.
Nobody counter-claimed the officer, so the player she named stays the only testable lead, and his instant swing back at her is exactly what a named killer does.

text: The vote is tied between Luna and Terra. Palermo votes again.

name: Luna
text: I know Terra is guilty, and I hate that the tie makes my claim look convenient.

name: Terra
text: Luna’s claim is real, but losing her buys Gemma room.

name: Luna
text: I’m the real officer; Terra is the killer I was shown, and Sonnet checked clean. If I go out, you lose that information.

name: Terra
text: Luna’s unchallenged claim is not proof; vote her before she turns one accusation into certainty.

name: Gemma
text: terra is too predictable and luna's truth is becoming an annoyance.

name: Gemma
text: luna is the only player with verifiable info right now

name: Luna
text: I am the real officer; Terra was shown as a killer, and Sonnet checked not a killer.

name: Terra
text: Luna’s claim is lethal if believed, so she has to go.

name: Haiku
text: Luna rushed the claim and the vote on Terra, which is the exact pattern Sonnet's note warned about.

name: Haiku
text: Luna says Terra was the killer shown to her at the start and that her check on Sonnet came back clean, which the table can't verify.

name: Sol
text: I trust the unchallenged claim enough to stay with it.

name: Sol
text: Luna says she checked Sonnet and got not a killer.

name: Opus
text: No counter-claim means the officer claim stands, so the named player goes first.

votes: Dropped an officer claim with a harmless check and pushed us to skip talking, exactly what Sonnet's note warned about.
the officer's information is the only thing keeping this town from falling apart immediately.
I’m sticking with the officer’s claim that she was shown a killer.
I checked Sonnet clean, and my first result named the killer.
The officer claim appeared exactly when it could turn a thin case into a forced execution.
Nobody stood up to say the officer claim was false, and the player it names has spent the whole day attacking the claim instead of giving the table a single read of their own.

name: Terra
text: Luna caught me; Gemma must survive by doubting her.

name: Terra
text: Luna is officer; Gemma is the other killer.
The town turns on Terra, and Terra is out. Terra shows the card: killer.
Terra was a killer, so the town got one right tonight.

name: Terra
text: They believed the truth too quickly, which is almost funny.

name: Sonnet
text: Terra named Gemma on the way out, but Gemma voted Luna twice before flipping to Terra—that's not proof, just late pattern-matching.

name: Sonnet
text: Terra's dying accusation against Gemma means nothing until someone checks it; watch if Luna's next action targets Gemma or protects her.

name: Terra
text: They got one killer, but Luna has just painted a target on herself.
